summary.intent: Resolve merge conflicts on PR #467, open and describe PR #469 (Markdown module refactor), and then address Entire findings on change #77 while understanding why the agent's own checks were missing issues the Entire reviewer found.
summary.outcome: #467 was made mergeable (spec conflict resolved, history joined with the rebased remote via `-s ours`, pushed without force) and #469 was opened. A list-marker bug (tab or end-of-line after a marker rejected by the shared classifier) was fixed, verified by mutation testing, strengthened with a structured property test, committed and pushed. The user's question about why the agent misses these findings was not directly answered in the transcript.

repo: GitHub ruleset requires 1 approving GitHub review, dismisses stale reviews on push, requires thread resolution, allows only the merge method, and uses a merge queue. Entire approvals are Entire-only and do not satisfy it.

Entire's CLI cannot set change states: `trail update --status` is trail-level only, `trail merge` tries to merge, and `unlink` only detaches the branch. Changes #72-#74 stay `open` after their PRs merged.
Entire's `trail finding <id> --branch <b> --json` lists findings with severity, status and location.
Stacked PRs caused SHA divergence, conflicts in docs/specs/release.json, and merge-up commits; the user's rule is now independent PRs off main, one at a time.

Verification for release-related changes includes cargo clippy with -D warnings, cargo doc with RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings, cargo test on callisto-graph and callisto-cli, and the contract scripts under .github/actions/callisto-action/tests and .github/tests.
The repo is worked in a git worktree at .claude/worktrees/macos-15-runners.

code.finding: The shared list-marker classifier only accepted a space after the marker, so tab-separated ordered lists (`1.<tab>`) were misclassified as headlines. The fix accepts empty rest, space or tab, matching the classifier it replaced.
Added a property test comparing the new classifier against the old one, with a structured generator so it can generate inputs like `1.<tab>`. A purely random-string generator rarely hit that case.

workflow: Mutation-check new tests by reintroducing the bug. Doing so showed the property test alone did not catch it until the generator was made structured.
When a push is rejected, fetch and inspect the remote's commits and diff before discarding local work. Here the remote was a rebase with identical trees, so `merge -s ours` avoided a force push.
Use a differential property test (new implementation vs. the old one) with an explicit list of intended differences when consolidating duplicated logic.
Record process rules the user gives (like no stacking) as memory and supersede the older conflicting note.

friction: The remote branch of #467 had been rebased onto an older main, so the push was rejected and the merge conflicted.
Entire approvals do not show up as GitHub reviews, so #467 stays REVIEW_REQUIRED, and each push dismisses any prior approvals.
Entire change states (#72-#74) cannot be updated from the CLI, even though their PRs have merged.
The original property test had a weak random generator that missed the tab-after-marker regression, which the Entire reviewer then caught.
open_items: Report to Entire that merged changes #72-#74 remain `open`, or fix it through their UI or support.

Check whether Entire can mirror its approvals as GitHub reviews.
Other findings on #77 may remain beyond the list-marker fix, so recheck them.
